    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersAtlanta pimento cheese with crackersCheddar and roasted capsicum spread with crackersHow to make it200g vintage cheddar100g mayonnaise1 jar of roasted red capsicum1 tsp Worcestershire sauce1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/2 tsp paprika200g crackers1 bunch of celery1 jar of cornichonsFinely grate the cheddar.Mix with the mayonnaise, chopped capsicum, Worcestershire, cayenne and black pepper until combined but still chunky.Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.Spoon into a bowl, dust with paprika and serve with crackers, celery sticks and cornichons.Backyard brunch fried green tomatoesCornmeal crumbed green tomatoes fried crisp, with a buttermilk herb dressingHow to make it4 green tomatoes, thickly sliced250ml buttermilk100g fine polenta50g plain flour1 tsp smoked paprika125ml vegetable oil100g whole egg mayonnaise1 chives1 lemonSalt the tomato slices and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry.Dip each slice in 150ml of the buttermilk, then in the polenta, flour and paprika mixed.Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Drain.Whisk the rest of the buttermilk with the mayonnaise, chopped chives and a squeeze of lemon.Serve the tomatoes hot with the dressing.Prawn and grits cupsHenry married Tina. Eat your feelings.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsPark picnic ham and spinach frittataBaked frittata with ham, potato, spinach and fetaHow to make it300g potatoes1 onion1 tbsp olive oil150g leg ham100g baby spinach8 eggs100ml thickened cream100g feta100g rocket1 lemon1 jar of tomato relishDice the potato, onion and ham and crumble the feta.Boil the potato until tender, then drain.Fry the onion in oil in an ovenproof pan, add the potato, ham and spinach and stir until wilted.Whisk the eggs with cream and salt, pour over and scatter with feta.Cook on low heat until the edges set.Bake at 180°C until set and golden.Serve with rocket dressed in lemon and relish.Atlanta fried chicken and wafflesButtermilk fried chicken, waffles and hot mapleHow to make it8 chicken tenderloins250ml buttermilk1 tsp hot sauce150g plain flour1 tsp smoked paprika1 L vegetable oil, for frying250g self-raising flour2 eggs300ml milk60g butter, melted125ml maple syrup100g baby spinach1 lemonSoak the chicken in the buttermilk with the hot sauce and a pinch of salt for at least 1 hour.Whisk the self-raising flour, eggs, milk and melted butter into a smooth batter.Cook the waffles in a hot greased waffle iron until crisp and keep warm in a low oven.Dredge the chicken in the plain flour mixed with the paprika, salt and pepper, and fry at 170°C for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.Warm the maple syrup with a dash of hot sauce. Stack the chicken on the waffles, pour over the maple and serve with the spinach dressed in lemon juice and a little oil.SweetsStrawberry shortcake for MumScones with balsamic strawberries and creamHow to make it300g strawberries3 tbsp caster sugar1 tsp balsamic vinegar80g butter250g self-raising flour170ml full cream milk300ml thickened cream1 tbsp icing sugar1 tsp vanilla extractSlice the strawberries and toss with sugar and balsamic.Leave the strawberries to macerate for 20 minutes.Rub the cold butter into the flour and sugar, add milk and pat out to 2cm thick.Cut into rounds and brush with milk.Bake at 220°C until risen and golden.Whip the cream with icing sugar and vanilla.Split the shortcakes and fill with cream and strawberries.Breakfast in bed almond croissantsCroissants filled with almond cream, baked and dusted with icing sugarHow to make it180g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla extract80g butter1 egg100g almond meal4 croissants30g flaked almonds1 tbsp icing sugar1 jar of strawberry jamSimmer the sugar, water and vanilla into a light syrup, then cool.Beat the butter, remaining sugar, egg and almond meal into a smooth paste.Split the croissants, brush the insides with syrup and spread with half the almond cream.Close the croissants, spread the rest of the almond cream on top and scatter with flaked almonds.Bake at 180°C until golden.Dust with icing sugar and serve with jam.DrinksMum's blood orange mimosaBlood orange juice, orange liqueur and sparkling wineHow to make it6 blood oranges40ml orange liqueur750ml sparkling wine500ml soda waterJuice the oranges and strain.Pour juice and orange liqueur into each flute.Slowly top with chilled sparkling wine and garnish with an orange wheel.For the kids, mix the leftover juice with soda water.Iced hibiscus tea with mintFor the folks, rolling up in the RV.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
